max_tire.note: Jeep-CJ.com consensus on a 15x8 wheel; one owner reports 32x11.50s with 'very little rubbing', but 32s generally need tired springs. Stock gearing and brakes feel it
Fits for mild use; reset the steering stops or the tires hit the leaf springs at full lock, and expect contact when the suspension is stuffed
The comfortable trail setup for 33s (one 4 in owner still wanted more stuff room); regear from the stock 3.55 or 3.73 ratios

items.title: Steering gear
items.summary: Campaign on the steering gear box of 18,858 1976 CJ-5 and CJ-7s; NHTSA's online record names the component but carries no defect summary.

items.title: Electronic ignition wire connectors
items.summary: Connectors could not carry enough current for the electronic ignition control.

items.title: Transmission adapter-plate seal
items.summary: A mis-seated seal could let gear oil migrate from the manual transmission into the transfer case; 96,933 CJs covered.

items.title: Intermediate steering-shaft coupling
items.summary: Oversized serrations could stop the coupling clamping properly to the steering-gear shaft, causing free play.

items.title: Tie-rod adjuster clamp bolts
items.summary: Loose clamp bolts on the connecting-rod adjuster tube could shift the steering-wheel position and risk loss of steering.

items.title: Transmission-to-transfer-case gasket
items.summary: Wrong gasket could block lubricant flow and damage the manual transmission.

items.title: Rear seat-belt buckles missing
items.summary: Some Jeeps got two tongue-end rear belt halves and no buckle, so the rear belts could not be fastened.

items.title: Automatic throttle-control rod spring
items.summary: Improperly installed spring could make the throttle close slowly.

items.title: Manual transmission first-gear lubrication
items.summary: Factory-fill gear oil might not protect first gear; covered 1982 CJ-5, CJ-7, Cherokee, Wagoneer and J-trucks.

timeline.change: CJ-7 launches on a 93.5 in wheelbase with doors, optional molded hardtop and steel doors, and optional full-time Quadra-Trac (with the TH-400 automatic). Dana 20 transfer case, narrow-track Dana 30 / AMC 20 axles
AMC 304 V8 available (3.55 axles); it goes away after 1981, leaving the 258 six as the top engine
Golden Eagle package (304 V8) arrives, running through 1980
The 258 six replaces the 232 as the standard engine; last year of the Dana 20, Quadra-Trac, the T-150 and the T-18
Dana 300 transfer case replaces the Dana 20 on every CJ-7; Laredo trim debuts; Golden Hawk sticker package for one year. Export-only Isuzu C240 diesel runs 1980–82
Wide-track Dana 30 front and AMC 20 rear replace the narrow-track axles; 630 numbered Jamboree Editions and the 1982–83 Limited (2,500 built)
Canadian Army takes 195 militarised CJ-7s as a stop-gap between the M38A1 and the Iltis
Final year; some late trucks get a wide-track Dana 44 rear in place of the two-piece AMC 20 as supplies run out, and the last run wears the 'Last of a Great Breed' dash plaque

identify.intro: CJ-7s have been re-engined, re-axled and re-badged for 40 years, and plenty of 'Renegades' and 'Laredos' are sticker jobs, so trust the VIN, the axle tags and the body measurements over the decals.

items.head: Body and wheelbase
items.body: 93.5 in wheelbase, 55 in windshield, about 81 in from the door hinge to the rear of the tub, and a 'U'-shaped door opening rather than the CJ-5's inverted 'S'. A CJ-8 looks the same up front but has a 103.5 in wheelbase and a longer rear.

items.head: VIN format
items.body: 1976–80 trucks carry a 13-character Jeep VIN; 1981–86 use the 17-character federal format. On 1981–86 VINs the 4th character is the engine (B = 151 Iron Duke, C = 258 six, H = 304 V8, U = AMC 150 four, F = Isuzu diesel), the 5th the transmission/transfer case, characters 6–7 read 87 for a CJ-7, and the 10th is the model year (B = 1981 … G = 1986).

items.head: VIN plate locations
items.body: Main riveted tag on the driver's side firewall near the master cylinder; a partial VIN is stamped on the passenger-side frame rail above the rear wheel. Make sure the tag and the frame stamping agree: a mismatch can mean a swapped tub or a salvage rebuild.

items.head: Axles
items.body: 1976–81 narrow-track Dana 30 / AMC 20; 1982–86 wide-track versions; a factory Dana 44 rear only on some late-1986 trucks (and, per Offroaders.com, on some Quadra-Trac trucks as a narrow-track, offset Dana 44). Any other Dana 44 under a CJ-7 is probably an aftermarket swap.

items.head: Special editions
items.body: The 1982 Jamboree has a numbered dash plaque (630 built: 560 Topaz Gold Metallic, 70 Olympic White) and, per Wikipedia, is the only numbered AMC Jeep. The Laredo added highback leather buckets, tilt wheel and chrome bumpers, grille cover and mirrors; Golden Eagles were 304 V8 trucks.

capability.note: Wikipedia figure; varies with engine and top
Wikipedia's figures; Offroaders.com gives 3.54 (1976–79) and 2.73 (1980–86) as the common ratios, so read the axle code

values.intro: The busiest classic-Jeep market on Bring a Trailer. Original-engine Laredos and Renegades with the T-5 or T-18 and honest tubs set the pace, and swapped V8 and LS builds sell well if they're done right.

ranges.cond: Excellent / low-mile original or quality restomod

values.note: Compiled from Bring a Trailer CJ-7 results in October 2026 (about 83 sales, median around $19,000, middle half roughly $13,500–26,500). Swapped 401-, 5.3L- and LS-powered builds cluster in the mid-$30k to low-$40k range. Recheck current results before relying on these figures.
